guideTitle: The Best Ultrawide Monitors for Work, From Single-Cable Laptops to Two-Computer Desks
metaTitle: Best Ultrawide Monitors for Work: USB-C, KVM and Thunderbolt (2026)
metaDescription: We compared ultrawide monitors for office work on USB-C power delivery, KVM switching, Thunderbolt, Ethernet, eye-comfort modes and panel size, from 34-inch screens to 49-inch hubs.
introParagraphs: A work ultrawide earns its place through connectivity more than refresh rate. The features that change a working day are USB-C that charges a laptop over the same cable as the picture, a KVM switch or Thunderbolt dock that lets one keyboard and mouse serve two computers, and wired Ethernet through the monitor.

The other decision is size. A 34-inch 3440 x 1440 panel gives roughly the space of two smaller screens without a bezel; a 49-inch 5120 x 1440 panel gives more, but needs a wide, deep desk and more head movement to use the edges.
Our comparison is based on published specifications, warranty terms and price position, not hands-on testing. Prices range from about $205 to $1,230 at the time of writing.

sansui-34-curved-uwqhd.summary: A 34-inch 3440 x 1440 curved VA panel with PiP/PbP and wide color coverage for about $205.
sansui-34-curved-uwqhd.description:
The SANSUI is the low-cost way into a 34-inch ultrawide for work, and it is the most widely reviewed monitor here: a 3440 x 1440 curved VA panel with picture-in-picture and picture-by-picture for two sources at once.

SANSUI lists 97 percent DCI-P3 color and a 200Hz refresh rate, more speed than office work needs. Connections are two HDMI 2.1 ports and DisplayPort 1.4.

There is no USB-C, power delivery or KVM, so a laptop needs its own charger. If single-cable laptop charging matters, the LG 34WR55QK-B adds 65W USB-C for about $95 more at the time of writing.
sansui-34-curved-uwqhd.bestFor: Desktop users who want a 34-inch ultrawide for as little as possible.
sansui-34-curved-uwqhd.skipIf: You work from a laptop; the LG 34WR55QK-B charges it over USB-C.

lg-34wr55qk-b.summary: A 34-inch curved monitor with 65W USB-C, Reader Mode and a height-adjustable stand for about $300.
lg-34wr55qk-b.description:
The LG 34WR55QK-B is the sensible choice for most laptop users: 65W USB-C power delivery charges a typical work laptop over the same cable as the display, and the stand adjusts for height and tilt.

LG includes a Reader Mode, designed to reduce blue light for long reading and writing sessions, plus OnScreen Control software for arranging windows and PbP. It runs at 100Hz, which is plenty for office work.

There is no KVM, Thunderbolt or Ethernet, and 65W may charge higher-power laptops slowly under heavy load.
cons: 65W may be slow for high-power laptops
lg-34wr55qk-b.bestFor: Laptop users who want single-cable charging and an adjustable stand.
lg-34wr55qk-b.skipIf: You switch between two computers; the Samsung S95UA or Dell U4924DW have KVM switches.

dell-s3425dw.summary: A 120Hz 34-inch Dell with 65W USB-C, 99% sRGB and ComfortView Plus.
dell-s3425dw.description:
The Dell S3425DW is the step up if color accuracy matters: Dell lists 99 percent sRGB and 95 percent DCI-P3, alongside 65W USB-C and a 120Hz refresh rate.

ComfortView Plus is Dell's low-blue-light mode, and the Dell Premium Panel warranty covers the display. Its 0.03ms response time is the fastest here, though that matters more for games than work.

Like the LG, it has no KVM or Ethernet, and it costs about $80 more at the time of writing.
cons: Costs more than the LG for similar connectivity
dell-s3425dw.bestFor: Laptop users who review photos or design work and want better color on paper.
dell-s3425dw.skipIf: Color accuracy is not a priority; the LG offers the same 65W USB-C for less.

dell-u3425we.summary: The only Thunderbolt 4 monitor here, with 10 USB ports and Ethernet on a 120Hz IPS panel.
dell-u3425we.description:
The Dell UltraSharp U3425WE is the choice if you want the monitor to replace a docking station: it is the only Thunderbolt 4 monitor here, with 10 USB 3.2 Gen 2 ports and Ethernet built in.

The 3440 x 1440 IPS panel runs at 120Hz, and an ambient light sensor adjusts brightness through the day. PbP and a three-year warranty round it out.

It costs about $725 at the time of writing, far more than the other 34-inch monitors. If your laptop does not use Thunderbolt peripherals, the extra bandwidth may be more than you need.
cons: Power delivery wattage not listed here
dell-u3425we.bestFor: Professional desks with Thunderbolt laptops and many peripherals.
dell-u3425we.skipIf: You only need charging and a couple of ports; the LG or Dell S3425DW cost far less.

samsung-s95ua-49.summary: A 49-inch 120Hz business monitor with KVM, 90W USB-C and Ethernet.
samsung-s95ua-49.description:
The Samsung S95UA is the lower-cost route to a 49-inch work screen: 5120 x 1440 on a 1000R curve, with a built-in KVM switch, 90W USB-C power delivery and Ethernet.

The KVM lets one keyboard and mouse control two computers, and 90W charges higher-power laptops more comfortably than 65W. It runs at 120Hz with DisplayHDR 400 and a three-year business warranty.

A 49-inch screen needs a wide, deep desk, and using its edges involves more head movement. It costs several hundred dollars less than the Dell U4924DW at the time of writing.
samsung-s95ua-49.bestFor: Two-computer desks that want a 49-inch screen without paying the most.
samsung-s95ua-49.skipIf: Your desk is shallow or narrow; a 34-inch monitor is easier to live with.

dell-u4924dw.summary: A 49-inch IPS Black monitor with automatic KVM, 90W USB-C, 2.5GbE and 11 USB ports.
dell-u4924dw.description:
The Dell UltraSharp U4924DW is the most complete work hub here: a 49-inch 5120 x 1440 IPS Black panel with an automatic KVM switch, 90W USB-C, 2.5GbE Ethernet and 11 USB ports.

Dell lists 100 percent sRGB and dual 9W speakers. The IPS Black panel suits color-sensitive work better than the Samsung's VA panel.

It is the most expensive monitor here by a wide margin at the time of writing and has fewer buyer reviews than the others. It runs at 60Hz.
pros: Most ports and fastest Ethernet here
dell-u4924dw.bestFor: Professionals who want one screen and hub for two computers and many peripherals.
dell-u4924dw.skipIf: The Samsung S95UA's KVM, 90W USB-C and Ethernet cover your needs for much less.

buyingCriteria.explanation: 65W (LG, Dell S3425DW) covers many ultrabooks; 90W (Samsung S95UA, Dell U4924DW) gives more headroom for higher-power laptops. Check your laptop charger's wattage.
A KVM switch lets one keyboard and mouse serve two computers (Samsung S95UA, Dell U4924DW). Thunderbolt 4 (Dell U3425WE) turns the monitor into a full dock for a Thunderbolt laptop.
Wired networking through the monitor keeps a laptop to one cable. The Dell UltraSharps and Samsung S95UA include Ethernet.
Pixel density is similar (about 108 to 110 pixels per inch), so text sharpness is similar. The difference is width, desk space and head movement.
LG's Reader Mode, Dell's ComfortView Plus and the U3425WE's ambient light sensor adjust color temperature or brightness. They are conveniences rather than substitutes for good lighting and breaks.

faq.q: What's the best ultrawide for office work under $300?
faq.a: In this guide, the LG 34WR55QK-B, with 65W USB-C, a height-adjustable stand and Reader Mode. The SANSUI costs less but has no USB-C.

faq.q: Do I need a KVM switch?
faq.a: Only if you regularly use two computers at one desk. The Samsung S95UA and Dell U4924DW include one, which saves buying a separate switch.

faq.q: Is a 49-inch ultrawide better than a 34-inch for work?
faq.a: It gives more room for side-by-side windows but needs a wide, deep desk and more head movement. For focused writing or coding, a 34-inch screen may be easier to use all day.

faq.q: What USB-C wattage do I need?
faq.a: Match or approach your laptop charger's wattage. 65W suits many ultrabooks; 90W gives more headroom. Some high-power laptops draw more than 90W and may charge slowly or discharge under heavy load.

faq.q: Does a bigger ultrawide have sharper text?
faq.a: No. A 34-inch 3440 x 1440 panel and a 49-inch 5120 x 1440 panel have similar pixel density, so text looks similar.
The Dell UltraSharp U3425WE, which pairs it with 10 USB ports and Ethernet.

bottomLine: For most laptop users, the LG 34WR55QK-B is the place to start: 65W USB-C and an adjustable stand at a moderate price. The Dell S3425DW is worth paying more for if color accuracy matters, and the SANSUI suits desktop users on a budget.

For more complex desks, choose by connection. The Dell U3425WE replaces a Thunderbolt dock on a 34-inch screen; the Samsung S95UA adds a KVM and 90W USB-C at 49 inches; and the Dell U4924DW is the most complete, and most expensive, hub for two computers.
